evidence: Liv. 23.18.10: exercitus bonīs inexpertus atque īnsuētus (Lewis & Short: “unacquainted with, inexperienced in”)
terms.comment: With ab + ablative, in + accusative, or adversus; Lewis & Short: not in Cicero or Caesar.

terms.gloss: inexperienced in, unacquainted with, unskilled (+ genitive)
evidence: Caes. BG 4.22.1: hominēs barbarī et nostrae cōnsuētūdinis imperītī (Lewis & Short)
Sall. Jug. 49.2: utī prūdentēs cum imperītīs manūs cōnsererent (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: hominēs barbarī et nostrae cōnsuētūdinis imperītī
phrases.english: barbarians, and men unacquainted with our ways

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
